references.text: Parallel text in Deuteronomy where the first commandment is repeated: You shall have no other gods before me.
Warning against following other gods that expands on the meaning of the first commandment.
The Lord declares himself a jealous God who does not permit worship of other gods.
The Lord's declaration that there is no other God beside him.
God proclaims that he is the first and the last, and that there is no god besides him.
Hosea reminds the people that they shall know no other God but the Lord.
Jesus quotes the command to worship the Lord alone when he is tempted by the devil.
Paul confirms that there is only one God, the Father, and one Lord, Jesus Christ.
Affirms faith in one God and Father of all, who is over all and through all and in all.
Paul emphasizes that there is only one God and one mediator between God and mankind.
Specifies the first commandment by forbidding the making of idols as a form of having 'other gods'.
Wisdom reflection on the first commandment emphasizing the exclusivity of the relationship with God.
Prophetic application of the first commandment as the basis for God's judgment against covenant breaking.
Extends the first commandment to also include verbal acknowledgment of other gods' names.
The law in Leviticus links the identity of God directly to the prohibition against idolatry.
Prohibits entering into covenants that would imply recognition of other gods.
Historical memory of the covenant's requirements linking history with the first commandment.
Reiteration of the prohibition against idols as a direct consequence of the first commandment.
